title.narrative: Building the resilience of vulnerable populations in Niger through access to an integrated package of WASH services (2024-2026)

description.narrative:
The main objective of the project is to contribute to providing the Nigerien population with sustainably managed water supply and sanitation services in a context of climatic and security fragility taking into account the needs of IDPs.
This entails implementing a multifaceted and integrated approach that combines infrastructure development, community education, and sustainable practices to not only address immediate needs but also address long-term resilience. By deploying innovative approaches, and community-centered strategies, the project will create lasting impacts, empowering vulnerable populations to withstand and recover from emergencies while fostering sustainable development and growth.
The Project objective is in line with Niger’s National Humanitarian Plan and UNICEF’s Global Strategic Plan and Country Programme for 2023-2027 and the Danish Development Strategy: "The World We Share".
The objective also aligns with UNICEF’s vision for WASH, which is the realization of the human rights to water and sanitation for all. The project will contribute to two key objectives of the UNICEF strategy for water, sanitation and hygiene 2016-2030: 1. By 2030, achieve universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water for all; 2. By 2030, achieve access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene for all and end open defecation, paying special attention to the needs of women and girls and those in vulnerable situations.

This project is part of Denmark's commitment to investing in climate change adaptation initiatives for the benefit of vulnerable populations in Niger who are suffering from climatic hazards and the security crisis.
Continuing support for the water sector is justified by the vital and social nature of the water sector (drinking water, hygiene and sanitation and pastoral hydraulics), not only to improve the living conditions of internally displaced populations in the current fragile security context in Niger, but also by the fact that meeting these needs will help to minimize conflicts around access to water and ensure social cohesion. It is this humanitarian objective that guided Denmark's decision to finance this project implemented by UNICEF Niger.
The expected results of the project are as follows: • Outcome 1: People affected by humanitarian crises have access to integrated and vital WASH services • Outcome 2: people have improved access to multi-purpose, climate-resilient WASH services and livelihoods in vulnerable communities. • Outcome 3: Children in schools and patients and carers in health/nutrition centres have access to climate-sensitive WASH services • Outcome 4: The population of municipalities (in the Diffa and Tahoua regions) live in acceptable hygiene and sanitation conditions.
